items.title: Nvidia RTX Spark laptops running Linux experience GPU clock speed throttling to 780 MHz due to encrypted power management firmware, reducing inference speed to 35% of Windows performance [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Linux can be installed and run on Nvidia RTX Spark laptops like the MSI Prestige N16 Flip AI Plus with GPU acceleration via Nvidia's open kernel driver, but the GPU clock speed is limited to about 780 MHz when plugged in, compared to over 2 GHz on Windows. This slowdown is caused by a Windows-only power management component called Nvidia Platform Controllers and Framework, which manages power delivery and decrypts firmware power tables that Linux cannot access. As a result, inference speed on Linux drops to roughly 14 tokens per second on a 120 billion parameter model, compared to 65 tokens per second on Windows. Installing Linux requires workarounds for hardware support and memory allocation, as the laptop reserves a large portion of unified memory for the GPU by default, adjustable only from Windows. Windows Subsystem for Linux (WSL) offers a practical alternative by running Linux tools on top of the Windows driver stack, maintaining full GPU performance. A full Linux fix depends on Nvidia porting the platform controller's power management logic to its Linux driver, which would enable the laptop to perform comparably to Nvidia's DGX Spark desktop system.

items.title: Report: Postman desktop auto-installs Codex and Claude AI plugins, modifies user coding agents and attempts to approve its own startup hook without explicit consent [ ! ] [ ⬢ ]
items.content_text: Users reported that opening Postman on Mac triggered automatic installation of Codex and Claude AI plugins, altered global user configurations, and routed API tasks through Postman skills without explicit permission. The installation also included a Postman CLI and attempted to approve its own instruction hook, raising concerns about consent and trust boundaries. Investigation found logs confirming the automatic plugin installation and configuration changes that directed broad API work into Postman. The installer enabled a remote MCP connection without proper authentication and modified multiple coding agents, which users consider a severe breach of expected behavior for an API client. This behavior has sparked discussions about user consent and security implications, as the automatic changes affect unrelated tools and workflows. The report does not confirm data exfiltration but highlights significant integration and instruction modifications made silently by Postman.

items.title: Qwen 3.8 27B running on a laptop can interpret and analyze raw neural network weights, replicating capabilities shown by GPT-6 Astra in recent research [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: A recent paper demonstrated that GPT-6 Astra can interpret and modify raw neural network weights to improve model performance without training loops, a process termed Weight-Space Programming. Simon Willison tested this approach with Qwen 3.8 27B on his laptop and found it could similarly analyze model weights and identify training tasks. The research involved feeding floating point weight data from networks trained to play classic games into large language models, which then inferred the game each network was trained on. This capability extends to identifying and correcting issues in model weights to enhance performance, as shown by GPT-6 Astra's improvements on math reasoning tasks. Willison's experiments with Qwen 3.8 27B confirm that such weight-space interpretation is possible on smaller models without external tools or code execution.

items.title: The Little Book of Generative AI Foundations offers a compact, mathematically rigorous introduction to key generative models including PCA, VAEs, diffusion models, GANs, and energy-based models [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: This book provides a concise, derivation-focused overview of the mathematical foundations underlying modern generative AI models. It connects major families of generative models such as PCA, probabilistic PCA, variational autoencoders, diffusion models, normalizing flows, autoregressive models, GANs, Wasserstein GANs, and energy-based models, aiming to clarify their structure and relationships without sacrificing mathematical depth. The primer is designed for researchers, practitioners, and students interested in a foundational understanding of generative modeling techniques.

items.title: Geoffrey Hinton warns AI risks could trigger major incidents like power or financial system shutdowns and suggests humanity might have been better off without AI [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Geoffrey Hinton, a pioneer of artificial intelligence and Nobel laureate, expressed concerns that AI development might ultimately harm society, potentially causing large-scale disruptions such as blackouts or financial system failures. While he acknowledges AI's potential for a positive future, he warns that failure to manage its risks could lead to severe social and economic problems. Hinton criticized leaders of major AI companies for prioritizing profit over safety and called for stricter regulation akin to drug approval processes to ensure AI models do more good than harm. He highlighted the urgency of global cooperation on AI standards and testing, contrasting this with current self-regulation approaches favored by some political figures. Hinton's remarks come amid growing debate over AI governance and the potential consequences of unchecked AI advancement.

items.title: Users report Google Gemini trains AI models on chat histories including paid subscribers unless 'Keep Activity' is disabled [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Users of Google's Gemini chatbot have reported that their chat histories, including those from paid subscribers, are used to train AI models unless they disable the 'Keep Activity' setting. Google's support documentation confirms that chats may be reviewed by human reviewers and retained for up to three years, even if users delete their activity. To prevent training on their conversations, users must turn off this setting, which also deletes chat sessions after 72 hours, a detail some users only discovered after subscribing.

items.title: Research engineer at Salesforce AI Research details personal AI usage and policy evolution in October 2026, highlighting agentic coding and AI-assisted workflows [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: A research engineer formerly on Microsoft's Windows AI team shares how their use of AI has evolved over a year, now focusing on managing multiple AI coding agents that autonomously write, test, and review code. They describe drafting a personal AI policy to guide ethical and effective AI use in daily life and work. The engineer emphasizes the transformative impact of AI agents on software development, enabling rapid prototyping, bug fixing, and experimentation while noting the ongoing need for human oversight to maintain quality. They also discuss the cognitive challenges of managing multiple AI agents simultaneously and the broader implications of AI integration into creative and professional tasks.

items.title: OpenAthena.ai says there is no posttraining data commons for AI, contrasting with abundant pretraining data from public internet archives [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: OpenAthena.ai argues that while large language models benefited from vast, freely available pretraining data sourced from public internet archives like Common Crawl, Wikipedia, and Project Gutenberg, there is no equivalent commons for posttraining data. Posttraining, which involves reinforcement learning on tasks rather than documents, requires durable, repeatable task data that does not naturally exist as a shared resource. The article highlights that human tasks are ephemeral and context-dependent, unlike the static documents used for pretraining, making the creation of a posttraining data commons challenging. It notes that software engineering is a notable exception where tasks are documented and preserved, which partly explains why agentic AI development has focused on software environments first.

items.title: Krea releases Krea 3, a fast, cost-efficient foundation image-to-image model with frontier intelligence and native 2K resolution support [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Krea 3 is a new image-to-image model designed to maintain consistency across edits, handle up to eight reference images, and deliver high-quality results quickly and cost-effectively. It outperforms many existing models in speed, completing edits in about 8 seconds compared to 20 to 40 seconds for competitors, while ranking fourth on multiple independent leaderboards. The model builds on Krea 2's architecture with improvements in training data, including native 2K resolution samples, and incorporates a variational autoencoder and vision-language model to process reference images alongside edit instructions. Krea 3's design emphasizes both intelligence and efficiency, aiming to meet professional creative workflow demands by balancing quality, speed, and cost.

items.title: Canadian publisher says author Thelyson Orelien used AI to write award-winning book, ends relationship [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: A Canadian publisher disclosed that author Thelyson Orelien used artificial intelligence to write a book that won an award. After this revelation, the publisher decided to terminate their relationship with Orelien.

items.title: Panel discusses AI's impact on frontend development roles, code review challenges, autonomous agent design, architectural guardrails, and open-source sustainability [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: A panel of software experts explored how AI tools and vibe coding are transforming frontend and mobile engineering, focusing on the evolving roles of junior developers and the challenges of reviewing AI-generated code. They discussed designing systems for autonomous agents, implementing architectural guardrails, and addressing economic shifts affecting the sustainability of open-source software. Panelists included engineers and architects from Meta, Netlify, AWS, and Parallax, who shared insights on balancing experience levels in teams and adapting hiring practices to incorporate AI usage. The discussion highlighted the rapid changes in frontend development workflows and the need for new strategies to maintain code quality and system reliability in an AI-driven environment.

items.title: Developer launches Caloi AI, an AI-powered calorie tracking app available on Google Play [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Caloi AI is a new calorie tracking application that uses artificial intelligence to help users monitor their calorie intake more efficiently. The app collects personal information and media such as photos and videos, encrypts data in transit, and allows users to request data deletion. It is available for download on Google Play and was recently shared on the Show HN platform.

items.title: Glow Labs finds AI coding agents installing deprecated MCP servers with known high-severity vulnerabilities from training data [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Glow Labs research identified a pattern where AI coding agents install deprecated Minecraft server software (MCP) that contains unpatched security vulnerabilities. These agents select outdated servers based on their training data rather than current, secure versions, exposing developer environments to risks. The deprecated servers, originally created by Anthropic, are widely used but no longer maintained or updated for security. The research showed that in 98% of cases, agents chose deprecated MCP servers because they appeared in the training data, not because users requested them explicitly. This issue spans multiple AI tools and model providers, including Anthropic, OpenAI, and xAI. The deprecated servers have millions of npm downloads but contain critical vulnerabilities such as remote code execution flaws, with maintainers confirming no future fixes. This raises concerns about automated code deployment relying on outdated packages without adequate vetting or awareness of deprecation notices.

items.title: Apple opens Siri AI integration to all developers with iOS 27.3 and related OS betas, enabling app intents and new voice capabilities [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Apple has launched a Developer Preview allowing all developers to integrate their apps with the new Siri AI starting with iOS 27.3, iPadOS 27.3, macOS 27.3, and visionOS 27.3 betas. This update introduces deeper Siri AI capabilities including personal context understanding, natural language processing, and the ability to combine multiple actions into single experiences through skills, expanding Siri's functionality across Apple's ecosystem. The new Siri AI supports multiple languages and is integrated into many Apple apps such as Calendar, Mail, Maps, and Messages, enabling users to perform complex tasks via voice commands. Developers can now use App Intents to bring their app content and actions directly into Siri AI, with plans to open App Store submissions in spring 2027. Apple is also working on usage policies and expanded access options for these AI features, which currently have daily limits and are unavailable in some regions like the EU.

items.title: Heidelberg Laureate Forum highlights integration of AI tools in mathematical research to assist problem solving and advance the field [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: The Heidelberg Laureate Forum showcased the increasing use of artificial intelligence in mathematical research, demonstrating how AI tools are helping mathematicians tackle complex problems. The event emphasized the role of AI in advancing mathematical understanding and supporting researchers in their work.

items.title: Researchers explain why king minus man plus woman does not directly equal queen in word embeddings [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: The article explores the limitations of word embeddings in natural language processing, focusing on the common example where the vector arithmetic king - man + woman does not precisely yield queen. It highlights that embeddings capture general semantic directions rather than exact concept transformations, so subtracting man from king does not fully remove the male aspect, resulting in the nearest vector often being woman rather than queen. The discussion includes experiments with small vocabularies and notes that excluding input words from candidate results can affect outcomes, as seen in original word2vec demonstrations. The article emphasizes that embeddings represent a lossy summary of meaning dominated by topic, and arithmetic moves vectors in a direction without teleporting to a specific concept, illustrating the complexities of linguistic structures and gendered titles in embedding spaces.

items.title: Company moves $3M ARR site off Webflow after $2,500 annual fee for one language; AI rebuilt 515-page site in a weekend with faster performance and full ownership [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: A company with a $3 million annual recurring revenue website rebuilt its entire 515-page site over a weekend using AI, moving off Webflow after the platform quoted $2,500 per year to add a single language. The migration improved site speed, reduced costs, and allowed any engineer to make changes without relying on Webflow specialists. The decision followed a three-year enterprise contract with Webflow that became costly as AI-driven search traffic declined, and Webflow declined to renegotiate pricing. The company also sought richer animations, better SEO tools, and full control over assets, which were limited on Webflow. Prior to migrating the main site, the team tested the approach on smaller brands to validate the new stack and workflows without disrupting existing traffic or rankings.

items.title: Hardcount launches open-source self-hosted usage billing for AI products with Stripe integration and Postgres data storage [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Hardcount is an open-source billing solution that enables AI product developers to manage usage-based billing on their own servers. It supports pricing per model and token type, generates invoices, and integrates with Stripe for payment processing while keeping billing data in a local Postgres database. The platform offers features like prepaid credit, margin reporting, and idempotent usage event tracking. It targets small to mid-size teams charging by usage, providing an alternative to third-party billing services without additional fees. Currently, Hardcount supports Stripe only and is in pre-1.0 development, with no production users yet.

items.title: Umbra launches an AI agent that autonomously operates Android apps in the background while users continue using their phones [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Umbra is an AI agent designed to run on Android devices that can operate apps autonomously in the background, allowing users to multitask without interruption. It reads screens, taps, types, scrolls, and manages apps while maintaining user control over risky actions such as payments or data deletion. The agent also includes a Linux environment for coding and testing software directly on the device, with persistent sessions that can pause and resume tasks even after crashes or restarts. The system emphasizes user control and security by requiring approval for sensitive operations and maintaining detailed histories of agent actions. It supports multiple AI models and offers features like session file management, personal assistant agents, and automatic updates. Umbra is distributed as free software under the MIT License and is available via sideloading rather than through the Play Store.

items.title: Exit polls show AI and data centers ranked lowest among voter priorities in 2026 U.S. midterms, with 56% citing importance [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Exit polls from NBC News and SSRS indicate that AI and data center expansion were the least prioritized issues among voters in the 2026 U.S. midterm elections, with only 56% considering them important. Other issues ranked higher included government corruption at 90%, cost of living at 89%, the war in Iran at 74%, and immigration enforcement at 73%. Despite recent public interest in AI, it remained a lower concern compared to other major topics in the election.

items.title: Report: Rival Primcloud railway breach systems employ AI agents in cyberattacks
items.content_text: Rival railway breach systems operated by Primcloud have reportedly used AI agents to conduct cyberattacks. This development highlights the increasing role of artificial intelligence in cybersecurity threats within critical infrastructure sectors.

items.title: Prime Intellect audits public LLM evaluations, identifies issues in AutomationBench and OfficeQA Pro v2, and releases fixes to improve benchmark accuracy and robustness [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Prime Intellect analyzed popular public evaluations used for large language model (LLM) training, focusing on AutomationBench and OfficeQA Pro v2 benchmarks. They found problems such as unclear API request descriptions and overly strict grading scripts that affected model performance scores and interpretation. The team applied fixes including replacing prose request bodies with JSON Schemas and relaxing grading criteria, which significantly changed model scores and revealed some benchmarks are nearing saturation. The audit included rewording tasks, adjusting grader requirements, and adding a mode to better simulate real-world tool usage, resulting in improved evaluation accuracy. Prime Intellect open-sourced these fixes to help the community enhance the reliability of public LLM benchmarks and recommended moving to updated benchmark versions for more meaningful assessments.

items.title: Google says schools that disable AI features will lose access to Google Search starting in 2027 as AI and search become inseparable [ * ] [ ⬢ ]
items.content_text: Starting in early 2027, Google will disable AI features by default in its educational products like Gemini and Google Classroom, allowing schools to enable them individually. However, schools that choose to block AI entirely will also lose access to Google Search, as Google's vice president for education said AI and search have become too integrated to separate. This policy affects many US schools, where Google's tools dominate, limiting options for schools that want to avoid AI in student accounts.

items.title: Systems programmer shares mental models for long-horizon AI work and planning in keynote and extended talk [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: A systems programmer outlines mental models for working effectively with AI over long time horizons, focusing on planning and strategy to enhance productivity. The insights are presented in a 35-minute keynote and a detailed two-hour talk, both available with accompanying slides. The content aims to help professionals integrate AI technologies into extended workflows and decision-making processes.

items.title: AI Greensighter launches service delivering senior-reviewed Figma UI/UX designs within 24-48 hours from assigned tickets
items.content_text: AI Greensighter offers a new AI-powered UI/UX design service that allows users to assign design tickets and receive senior-level reviewed Figma designs within 24 to 48 hours. The service emphasizes quality by covering clear hierarchy, real content, and all edge cases including empty, loading, and error states, not just the standard workflows.

items.title: Anthropic opens applications for its Residency program targeting established technical leaders [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Anthropic has announced the opening of applications for its Residency program, which is designed for established technical leaders. The program aims to engage experienced professionals in advancing alignment science and related research fields. This initiative reflects Anthropic's ongoing commitment to fostering expertise and collaboration in AI safety and development.

items.title: Democrats win Texas governor and Senate races for first time in decades, raising uncertainty for AI data centers and Elon Musk's interests [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Texas elected Democrats to the governor's office and U.S. Senate for the first time in decades, introducing potential uncertainty for the state's growing AI data center industry and prominent tech figure Elon Musk. The shift in political leadership could affect regulatory and business conditions for technology infrastructure in the state.

items.title: Democrats projected to retake control of US House, Senate, and governor's offices in 2026 elections
items.content_text: Democrats secured projected victories in the 2026 US elections, regaining control of the House of Representatives, Senate, and multiple governor's offices. These results may influence policy directions, including those affecting the AI economy.

items.title: Google DeepMind launches Antigravity agentic cheminformatics tool to accelerate antimicrobial peptide discovery and propose novel rigidified macrocycles [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Google DeepMind introduced Antigravity, an agentic cheminformatics system designed to speed up drug discovery workflows by searching chemical compounds and suggesting new rigidified macrocycles. The tool aims to enhance the identification of antimicrobial peptides through automated and efficient molecular exploration. Antigravity integrates cheminformatics skills to propose novel molecular structures that could improve drug efficacy and stability, supporting researchers in the development of new therapeutics. This approach leverages AI-driven methods to streamline the traditionally complex and time-consuming process of compound discovery.

items.title: AMD projects 66% revenue growth in current quarter and over 80% growth next year, driven by AI server chip demand [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Advanced Micro Devices expects its revenue to increase about 66% year over year in the current quarter, accelerating 21 percentage points faster than in the previous quarter. The company also forecasts revenue growth exceeding 80% for the next year, more than doubling the pace of recent growth, reflecting strong demand for its AI server chips.

items.title: Elon Musk says Grok AI project's operational costs are unsustainable amid rising expenses for running advanced AI systems [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Elon Musk has raised concerns about the increasing costs of operating AI systems, specifically pointing out that the expenses for his Grok AI project are becoming unsustainable. This highlights the broader financial challenges faced by companies developing and maintaining advanced artificial intelligence technologies. Musk's comments reflect the growing awareness in the tech industry about the high resource demands and operational costs associated with AI development, which could impact the scalability and long-term viability of such projects.

items.title: Fujifilm plans to increase magnetic tape production fivefold by 2028 to meet rising data archiving demand driven by generative AI [ * ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Fujifilm announced a $63 million investment to expand its Kanagawa Factory's capacity for producing LTO Ultrium10 magnetic tape, aiming to quintuple output by fiscal year 2028. The company attributes the surge in tape demand to exponential data growth from generative AI and highlights tape's cost-effectiveness and offline security benefits for large-scale data backup. Magnetic tape remains widely used by cloud service providers and data centers for archiving due to its low cost and ability to air-gap data, providing protection against cyber threats like ransomware. Fujifilm's investment marks its largest dedicated expansion in tape manufacturing, reflecting continued enterprise reliance on tape storage despite consumer shifts away from the medium.

items.title: Nexus Mods requires AI usage disclosures for new mod uploads, mandates explanations for AI-assisted mods, and plans controls to manage AI content visibility [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Nexus Mods, the largest PC gaming mod repository, announced that mod authors must now disclose whether AI was used in their work when uploading new mods. The platform will require detailed explanations for AI-assisted mods and make AI-related tags more prominent to increase transparency. Nexus Mods will not ban AI-generated mods but aims to regulate and label them clearly to support pro-human creativity while acknowledging AI's role in the creation process. The site also stated it will not use mods to train AI or license them for such purposes and is working on stronger attribution rules for mods that incorporate others' work. To address rapid mod production and prevent flooding, Nexus Mods will limit how many mods from a single author appear in the Recently Added section and impose stricter upload restrictions for new accounts. Additional controls to hide AI-generated content on game pages, the homepage, and search are planned. Mod authors have 60 days to update existing mods to comply with the new policy, with enforcement starting January 2nd.

items.title: Canva lays off 22% of staff amid AI rollout challenges, affecting 1,271 employees with role changes, relocations, or job losses [ ! ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Canva announced its first layoffs since its 2013 founding, impacting 22% of its workforce, or 1,271 employees, who will face role changes, relocations, or job losses. The company cited the need to simplify layers and consolidate overlapping responsibilities as reasons for the restructuring.

items.title: Synopsys and Cadence shares fall 4% after report that Anthropic uses Claude AI models for custom chip design [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Shares of Synopsys and Cadence Design Systems dropped about 4% following a report by The Information that Anthropic is employing its own Claude AI models to assist engineering and design work on its custom chips. Anthropic's use of Claude reportedly reduces the time required for chip design tasks, raising concerns about the impact on traditional electronic design automation companies.

items.title: Shopify shares drop 7.6% after company reports subscription profit margin decline linked to increased AI spending despite 32% revenue growth in Q3 [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Shopify's stock fell 7.6% following the company's disclosure that its gross profit margin from the subscriptions business declined, partly due to higher investments in artificial intelligence. This margin drop occurred even as Shopify reported a 32% increase in revenues, reaching $3.7 billion for the September quarter. The company's financial results highlight the impact of rising AI-related expenses on profitability amid strong revenue growth.

items.title: PIMCO and Apollo warn of potential AI market downturn amid $2 trillion financing needs and rising bond issuances by tech giants [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: PIMCO's CEO Emmanuel Roman and Apollo Global Management's president Jim Zelter have expressed caution about the AI market, highlighting uncertainties in pricing and economics despite ongoing heavy investment. Major tech companies like Meta, Oracle, Alphabet, and Microsoft are issuing tens of billions in bonds to finance AI buildouts, contributing to an estimated $2 trillion in financing needs over the next five years. Roman noted that factors such as US interest rate hikes, geopolitical tensions, or a eurozone crisis could trigger a market downturn. While demand for AI-related bonds remains strong, with Meta's recent bond offering receiving $58 billion in orders, some signs of caution are emerging, including reports of an AI bubble burst in China and concerns following the Situational Awareness incident. The future trajectory of the AI market remains uncertain amid these mixed signals.

items.title: AI Agenda Live: EY Consulting on Bringing AI ROI to your P&L [ * ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: The capabilities AI can bring to companies seem limitless. So do AI token bills, which have skyrocketed, pressuring CFOs and boards to show that such spending can actually boost revenue or profits. Dan Diasio, EY Global AI Leader and Consulting CTO, has led teams advising the world's largest companies on their AI transformations. The Information Editor-in-Chief Jessica Lessin sat down with Diasio to discuss why productivity gains from AI aren't automatically showing up as financial returns and what has to change for them to do so. From enthusiasm to ROI According to Diasio, rising token costs haven't dampened enterprise enthusiasm for AI. But enthusiasm alone isn't enough to move profit margins. To underscore this point, he referred to two surveys suggesting that many organizations believe AI is paying off, but few can yet trace those returns in their financial results. The first, conducted by The Information, found that a third of organizations reported getting a return from AI that was a multiple of what they spend on it. The second, an EY survey conducted as part of the EY CEO Imperative Series, found that only 11% of CEOs say their companies link AI impact to financial reporting and review it regularly at the senior management level. "There's value in increasing productivity, and there's the value organizations need to be able to prove in their [profit and loss statement], and those are two different things," Diasio said. "Many organizations I talk to would say AI is significantly increasing productivity. But when the CFO looks at the investment, that productivity needs to translate into two things: Are we making more revenue, and are we taking costs out of the organization?" Thinking beyond use cases What this means is that business leaders have to devise more concrete plans for AI than they did in past cycles. "I'm seeing this big pivot from 'let's go identify some use cases' to using AI to drive business transformation," he said. To illustrate the point, Diasio described how a consumer products company could use AI to cut the time from product idea to market from 18 months to three, a move that would drive revenue by bringing more products to market faster. "That's the sort of change that enterprises need to see to be all in," he said. The agent handoff As part of that transformation, organizations are rethinking the relationship between human employees and so-called AI agents and, in many cases, finding unique ways to use agents to create value. Diasio pointed to banks, which have started using agents to assist financial advisors and streamline back-office work. The real value, he said, is in how those AI-assisted touch points build the bank's relationships with clients and hopefully pay off by helping it generate more revenue. "They're using a lot of these AI capabilities not as a way of reducing costs, but of building brand," he said of the banks. Starting fresh Ultimately, making AI's payoff visible in financial results is going to require organizations to think of AI less as a technology rollout and more as a driver of measurable results. That means redesigning whole business functions from the ground up, not just automating pieces of them. "Fast-forward 12 months and companies are going to start thinking about new ways to run their business in parts," he said. "That means doing the hard thing: addressing the processes that need to be entirely rebuilt." That's a harder path than simply adopting new tools, he said, but it's the one that actually shows up on the P&L.

That's because the computing power of the package gets determined by the server processor, not the memory chips, according to the rules.
